summary: iter98 (LiveToaster + AdminQueue live prepend) end-to-end tested with two browser contexts (admin viewing /admin/queue + client/vip posting new orders/withdrawals). 7/9 acceptance criteria PASS. One CRITICAL backend bug found: order_status_changed / withdrawal_status_changed are published ONLY to user_id=owner, so admin subscriptions never receive them and rows do NOT disappear from /admin/queue when items leave pending — this breaks half of the '/admin/queue live' feature.

critical.issue: Backend publishes `order_status_changed` (routes/admin.py:268) and `withdrawal_status_changed` (routes/admin_withdrawals.py:151) with user_id=target_uid only. `live_bus.publish()` treats user_id and roles as mutually exclusive (services/live_bus.py:120), so admin/employee subscriptions on /live/stream never receive these events. Consequence: rows in AdminQueue.jsx are never removed after approve/reject/complete/pay. The client-side toast for order approval still works because it is user-scoped.

integration_issues.issue: AdminQueue.jsx correctly listens for order_status_changed / withdrawal_status_changed but never receives them (see backend critical bug above). Frontend code path is fine; needs backend fix.

action_items: MAIN AGENT: Fix admin queue row-removal SSE. Two options: (A) In routes/admin.py after live_publish('order_status_changed', ..., user_id=target_uid), add a second call: `await live_publish('order_status_changed', {...}, roles=('admin','employee'))`. Do the same in routes/admin_withdrawals.py:151 for withdrawal_status_changed. (B) Or extend services/live_bus.publish() so a single call can target both `user_id` AND `roles`. Option A is safer/smaller change.

Optional: verify TOTP-gated rate update throttle end-to-end (test agent hit 422 because I didn't send the full ExchangeRateCreate payload — rates_updated broadcast code itself looks correct and is user_id=None so it will fan out; the 30s throttle in LiveToaster.jsx is straightforward and unit-testable).
critical_code_review_comments: LiveToaster.jsx (124 LOC): clean, focused, correctly gates admin toasts with `isStaff = ['admin','employee'].includes(user?.role)`. Throttle uses lastByKeyRef.current keyed by event type — 30s for rates / 10s for balance are per user session, which is exactly what the spec asked for. Passes.

AdminQueue.jsx: prepend logic guards against dupes with prev.orders.some(x => x.id === o.id). Good. Flash timeout cleanup on unmount via flashTimeoutsRef.current is correct. CSS injected inline via <style> works but polluting global CSS on every mount is slightly ugly — could be moved to App.css. Non-blocker.

services/live_bus.py:114-121: publish() branches on `if user_id is None` — meaning `user_id + roles` are mutually exclusive. This design forces the bug described above. If the intent is 'target the owner AND admins', publish() should accept both and union the two target sets. Suggested minimal patch: after computing targets when user_id is set, ALSO include broadcast_subs filtered by roles when roles is not None. Or dual-publish in the routes (simpler).

routes/admin.py:268 and routes/admin_withdrawals.py:151 both explicitly say '# iter97 — SSE push to the order OWNER' — so iter98's admin-queue removal was never wired in on the publish side. This is a design gap between iter97 and iter98.

AdminQueue.jsx handler for order_status_changed reads `payload.order_id` (correct — matches backend). For withdrawal_status_changed reads `payload.withdrawal_id` (also correct). No frontend fix needed once backend broadcasts.

Toast text respects i18n — verified both 'Nueva orden pendiente' (es) and 'New pending order' (en) work; admin test user's stored preference happens to be `en` so the browser showed English despite the request stating Spanish should be default. Not a bug in this iter, just an admin_seed preference.

Withdrawal row removal on status change: not directly tested at status transition, but same code path (routes/admin_withdrawals.py:151 uses user_id=target_uid) — will fail identically per the RCA.
rca_of_the_issue: services/live_bus.publish() at line 114 branches on `if user_id is None` — when user_id is set, roles filter is ignored and only per-user subscriptions receive the event. Admin queue subscribes as an admin broadcast subscriber (with role='admin' stamped in iter98) but is NOT in the per-user subscription map for arbitrary client user_ids. Backend fix: in routes/admin.py:268 and routes/admin_withdrawals.py:151, publish twice — once to the owner and once to admin/employee roles — OR extend live_bus.publish() to union both target sets when both user_id and roles are provided.
